question: What will the Antarctic sea ice extent be on October 10, 2026, according to the NSIDC Sea Ice Index?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the daily Antarctic sea ice extent for 2026-10-10 in the NSIDC Sea Ice Index version 4 daily file (S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv), in millions of square kilometers.
research:
I couldn't find any forecasts or markets on this. Through September 11 the 2026 extent was tracking 2025 almost exactly. If you apply the September 11 to October 10 changes from 2019-2025 to this year's value, you get about 16.79 to 17.55 million km² for October 10. That range is inside the question's 16.5 to 18.5 window.

## 1. Resolution source
- I read the NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4 southern daily CSV (S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv) directly. [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- Latest values published by the cutoff (the file usually lags by about one day), in million km²:
  - 2026-09-08: 17.460
  - 2026-09-09: 17.568
  - 2026-09-10: 17.565
  - 2026-09-11: 17.619
  - 2026-09-01: 17.415, for comparison. [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- These are single-day numbers, not 5-day averages, and they can jump by 0.1 or more from one day to the next.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. On 2026-09-11 the extent was 17.619, about the same as 2025 on that date (17.612). [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- The annual Antarctic maximum usually comes between early and late September. After it, the extent falls through October.

## 3. Recent news
- Early Sept 2026: Copernicus said August's average Antarctic extent was about 17.0 million km² (on its own dataset, not NSIDC's). That was about 6.5% below the 1991-2020 average and the 4th-lowest August on record. The biggest shortfalls were in the Amundsen Sea and the Indian Ocean sector. [Copernicus](https://climate.copernicus.eu/sea-ice-cover-august-2026)
- 2026-08: the Met Office (using the OSI SAF dataset) put extent on 2 August at 16.65 million km², the 4th-lowest for that date. [Met Office](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
- 2026-08-09 to 08-12: the NSIDC daily series dipped from 16.34 to about 15.96 in the middle of August, then rose quickly to 17.33 by 08-31. [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)

## 4. Base rates
Daily NSIDC v4 values, in million km², taken from the same CSV:

| Year | Sep 11 | Sep max (date) | Oct 10 | Change, Sep 11 to Oct 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 18.299 | 18.489 (Sep 26) | 18.234 | -0.065 |
| 2020 | 18.829 | 19.062 (Sep 25) | 18.659 | -0.170 |
| 2021 | 18.716 | 18.814 (Sep 1) | 17.889 | -0.827 |
| 2022 | 18.112 | 18.276 (Sep 13) | 17.898 | -0.214 |
| 2023 | 17.004 | 17.109 (Sep 7) | 16.508 | -0.496 |
| 2024 | 17.209 | 17.283 (Sep 15) | 16.861 | -0.348 |
| 2025 | 17.612 | 17.854 (Sep 15) | 17.301 | -0.311 |

- In all 7 years the extent was lower on October 10 than on September 11. The mean change was about -0.35 (median -0.31), ranging from -0.07 to -0.83.
- Applying those changes to 2026's 17.619 gives about 16.79 to 17.55. The median change gives about 17.31 and the mean about 17.27.
- The trend since 2023 is a step down from the 2019-2022 level. Oct 10 values from 2023 to 2025 were 16.51 to 17.30; from 2019 to 2022 they were 17.89 to 18.66. 2026 is running roughly level with 2025, above 2023 and 2024, and well below 2019 to 2022.
- Day-to-day noise is about ±0.05 to 0.1, and that matters for a single-day question.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I didn't search Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold specifically, and the searches I did run turned up no market or expert forecast for Antarctic extent on Oct 10, 2026.
- I also found no NSIDC or other official outlook for October Antarctic extent.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- When the annual maximum happens: if it comes late in September, October 10 could stay high, as in 2019 and 2020. An early peak followed by fast retreat, as in 2021, would push it down.
- Storms and winds in the Southern Ocean: pressure systems like the Amundsen Sea Low can compress or spread the ice edge by a few tenths of a million km² within days, as the mid-August 2026 dip showed.
- NSIDC's early-October Sea Ice Today post and the Met Office and Copernicus September reports will come out before the question resolves.
- I found no official seasonal sea-ice outlook covering September to October 2026 for Antarctica.

Sources:
- [NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4 southern daily CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/south/daily/data/S_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- [Copernicus, Sea ice cover August 2026](https://climate.copernicus.eu/sea-ice-cover-august-2026)
- [Met Office, Arctic and Antarctic sea ice briefing, August 2026](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
